audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may include cash economically owned by non-controlling interests
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash to parent equity without removing the portion attributable to joint-venture partners.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had total cash and equivalents of $773 million, including $2 million of restricted cash and $104 million of cash attributable to the Company's joint venture partners should the Company elect to issue cash dividends.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the latest filing identifies $94m of cash attributable to joint-venture partners, while the valuation adds the full $648m unrestricted balance. Removing $94m lowers base value from $112.90 to approximately $109.56 per share and narrows the premium over the $102.64 market price from $10.26 to $6.92. Any distribution taxes remain unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Disaggregate the June 30, 2026 cash by legal entity, remove the filed $94m partner-attributable amount, determine applicable withholding or distribution taxes, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Parent-attributable earnings may be combined with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with consolidated depreciation, amortization, capital expenditures, and potentially other cash-flow adjustments in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As the Company has one reportable segment, net sales, total assets, depreciation, amortization and capital expenditures are equal to consolidated results.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its net effect is not. Adding consolidated depreciation can overstate parent owner earnings, while subtracting consolidated capital expenditure can understate it. The filings show 2025 non-controlling-interest income of $12m, dividends to non-controlling interests of $21m, and non-controlling-interest equity of $83m, but do not allocate the relevant depreciation and reinvestment adjustments, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild each owner-earnings year using parent-attributable depreciation, amortization, capital expenditure, working-capital changes, and other adjustments, or use consolidated earnings and explicitly deduct the non-controlling interests' economic share; then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized commercial payments may be missing from required reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $92m net asset increase in 2025 and $42m additional increase in H1 2026; recurring cash outlay unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring commercial payments necessary to obtain or retain programs would reduce owner earnings if they are not already included in capital expenditures or another reinvestment deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Contractual payments represent certain amounts associated with commercial arrangements that are capitalized and subsequently recognized over the period to which they relate.
audit_findings.explanation: Omission is not yet demonstrated, because the record does not separately identify cash additions, amortization, acquisition effects, or where the payments enter the owner-earnings calculation. Nevertheless, contractual-payment assets increased from $26m to $118m in 2025 and to $160m by June 2026. The 2025 increase alone equals 51% of the $180.1m anchor, making the issue reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the contractual-payment asset rollforward and cash-flow classification for 2025 and H1 2026, isolate recurring cash additions from acquisitions, currency and amortization, deduct any amount absent from owner earnings, and rerun normalized OE and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The pension deficit is an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $50m gross deficit, or $1.78 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded pension obligation is a senior claim that should be reflected either through normalized funding in owner earnings or as an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has approximately $50 million in unfunded net pension liabilities as of December 31, 2025, of which approximately $38 million and $12 million are attributable to U.S. and non-U.S. pension plans, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated at December 31, 2025, but the filed $50m gross deficit is only 1.6% of the $3,178m base equity value. A full dollar-for-dollar deduction would reduce base value from $112.90 to approximately $111.12 per share, still $8.48 above the $102.64 market price. The latest filing does not provide a June 2026 funded-status calculation, so subsequent movement is unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Update the funded status at June 30, 2026 and document whether normalized OE includes deficit-funding contributions; deduct the after-tax deficit if not, but reopen materiality only if the updated claim is substantially larger than $50m.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may retain favorable one-time operating items
audit_findings.magnitude: $148m revenue bucket; one-time profit and OE contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any non-recurring operating profit retained in the $180.1m anchor is grown and capitalized through both the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Other cost performance, design changes and other increased net sales by $148 million primarily due to one-time items and sales from the recently acquired engineering services companies.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $148m sales increase within cost performance, design changes and other arose primarily from one-time items and acquired-company sales, but it does not disclose their separate profit contributions or establish whether the OE calculation normalized them. Under the existing model, a computed reduction of approximately $20.6m to anchor OE would eliminate the base-case premium over the market price, so the undisclosed one-time contribution is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the $148m revenue-bucket components and associated gross profit, taxes and cash effects; remove non-recurring settlements and recoveries from 2025 OE while retaining recurring acquisition economics and recurring costs, then rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-outs may be omitted claims against common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $22m original combined maximum; $7m paid in H1 2026; at most $15m remaining, or $0.53 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected unpaid contingent acquisition consideration is a claim against common equity if related acquired earnings are included but the payment is absent from owner earnings and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On May 21, 2025, Visteon acquired all equity shares of a user experience electronics engineering consulting and consumer research company for cash of $55 million ("UX Acquisition") not including contingent consideration of up to $9 million to be paid if certain financial and operational milestones are achieved.
audit_findings.explanation: The original UX and German acquisition caps total $22m, but $7m was paid during H1 2026 and is already reflected in the latest cash balance used by the valuation. Even treating the remaining $15m maximum as an immediate bridge deduction would reduce base value by only about $0.53 per share, or 0.5% of base equity value, and would not change the comparison with the $102.64 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 30, 2026 recorded fair value and remaining contractual maximum for the UX and German earn-outs and verify that the $7m payment is included in the cash rollforward; document the residual as immaterial unless additional contingent obligations exist.
